key_insight: PINNs miss shocks in steady inviscid flow because the steady Euler residual alone is too weak, so the model drifts to a smooth solution; adding pseudo-time evolution encourages shock formation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable PINN strategy for airfoil aerodynamics and other high-speed flow problems where capturing discontinuities is essential.
method: Recast steady shock-capturing as an unsteady Euler evolution problem.
Add time-derivative terms and a pseudo-time-stepping PDE loss to guide the network toward the steady state.
Use a simplified Euler formulation to improve shock-capturing accuracy.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on four forward problems with different flow conditions and geometries.
watch_item: Pseudo-time training can still be challenging for long-horizon unsteady evolution, so stability and computational cost may become important implementation concerns.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for shock capturing in inviscid flows around an airfoil
